title: still, yet, already and anymore
summary: Bốn từ nhỏ quyết định sắc thái thời gian: tiếp diễn, đã đổi, chưa xảy ra, sớm hơn dự kiến.
whyItMatters: Đây là nhóm từ band 7 hay dùng sai vì tiếng Việt gộp chúng vào *vẫn*, *đã*, *chưa*. *Still* không phải *yet*, *already* không phải *just*. Trong Task 2, câu như *The gap **still** persists despite a decade of funding* hay *Governments have **yet** to address the cause* thể hiện chính xác mức độ và thời gian — đúng thì rất band 8, sai thì người đọc hiểu ngược ý.

sections.heading: still: the situation has not changed
body: **Still** says a situation continues, often longer than expected: *The waiting list is still growing.* It sits in **mid position** — before the main verb, after *be*, after the first auxiliary: *She **still** works there*, *She is **still** working there*, *She has **still** not replied*.
**Still** also means *in spite of that*: *The scheme has been criticised for years, but it is still in force.* Here it marks contrast with the previous clause, not duration.
**Still + negative** expresses surprise or impatience, stronger than *yet*: *I sent the invitation weeks ago and he **still** hasn't replied.*

examples.right: The city is still short of affordable housing.
examples.wrong: Still the city is short of affordable housing.

examples.right: Despite repeated warnings, the practice still continues.
examples.note: *In spite of that* meaning — contrast, not duration.

examples.right: She still hasn't answered my email.
examples.note: **still + negative** = impatience; compare *She hasn't answered yet* (neutral).

sections.heading: not ... any more, not ... any longer, no longer
body: To say a situation **has changed**, use **not … any more** or **not … any longer**, both at the **end** of the sentence: *Lucy doesn't work here any more.* *The factory is not operating any longer.*
**No longer** carries the same meaning in **mid position**, and it is the most formal option: *Lucy no longer works here.* This is the version to use in academic writing.
Do not use **no more** in this sense: *We are no more friends* is wrong; write *We are no longer friends*. **Any more** is usually two words; *anymore* is accepted, especially in American English.

rows: The shop doesn't open on Sundays any more.
The scheme is not funded any longer.
The scheme is no longer funded.

sections.heading: yet: up to now, and still expected
body: **Yet** means *until now* and appears mainly in **negatives and questions**, usually at the **end**: *The report isn't finished yet.* *Have you decided yet?*

It pairs naturally with the **present perfect** because both look at a period leading to now: *Has the council approved the plan yet?* With *be* and states, the present simple is also common: *Is dinner ready yet?*
Two formal patterns are worth learning. **have yet to + verb** = have not yet done: *The government has yet to publish the figures.* **as yet** = so far: *As yet, no study has tested the claim.*

examples.right: The council has not published the figures yet.
examples.wrong: The council has not published the figures already.
examples.note: Negative + expectation → **yet**; *already* belongs to positive statements.

examples.right: The government has yet to explain the delay.
As yet, there is no evidence of a link.
examples.note: **as yet** = so far, used in academic prose.

sections.heading: already: sooner than expected
body: **Already** says something happened **earlier than expected**: *She has already left.* It goes in **mid position** or at the **end**: *She has left already.*
In **questions**, *already* signals surprise: *Have you finished already?* — the speaker expected it to take longer. Compare the neutral *Have you finished yet?*

Do not use *already* with a finished past time: *I already saw him yesterday* is acceptable in informal American English, but in IELTS Writing prefer *I had already seen him* or *I saw him yesterday*.

examples.right: By 2010, the city had already met its emissions target.
examples.wrong: By 2010, the city has already met its emissions target.
examples.note: A past deadline needs the past perfect **had already met**.

examples.right: Have you already read the report?
The technology is already cheaper than coal in most markets.

sections.heading: Contrasts that carry an argument
body: The four words form a small system. **Still** = it continues. **Yet** = it has not happened, but may. **Already** = it happened sooner than expected. **No longer** = it has stopped.

In Task 2, this system lets you describe policy failure precisely: *Enrolment **still** lags in rural districts, and the ministry has **yet** to explain why. Meanwhile, private tutoring has **already** become the default for urban families, so the public system is **no longer** the main provider.*
Note how the paragraph moves through time without a single explicit date. That is the kind of grammatical control that reads as band 8.

examples.right: The problem still exists, and no government has yet found a solution.
By the time the policy was reviewed, it had already been overtaken by events.
examples.note: **already** with past perfect for an earlier-than-expected event.

examples.right: Coal is no longer the cheapest source of electricity in most countries.

commonMistakes.wrong: Still I don't understand the second point.
commonMistakes.right: I still don't understand the second point.
commonMistakes.why: **still** đứng giữa câu, trước động từ chính (hoặc sau *be*), không đứng đầu câu như *however*.

commonMistakes.wrong: The country has not developed this sector already.
commonMistakes.right: The country has not developed this sector yet.
commonMistakes.why: Câu phủ định diễn tả *chưa* dùng **yet**, không dùng *already*. *Already* chỉ dùng trong câu khẳng định hoặc câu hỏi thể hiện ngạc nhiên.

commonMistakes.wrong: We are no more colleagues after the merger.
commonMistakes.right: We are no longer colleagues after the merger.
commonMistakes.why: **no more** không dùng với nghĩa *không còn nữa*. Dùng **no longer** (trang trọng) hoặc **not … any more** (trung tính).

commonMistakes.wrong: She doesn't work here no more.
commonMistakes.right: She doesn't work here any more.
commonMistakes.why: Câu đã có *doesn't* thì dùng **any more**, không dùng *no more* — tránh phủ định kép.

commonMistakes.wrong: By 2015, the city has already built three metro lines.
commonMistakes.right: By 2015, the city had already built three metro lines.
commonMistakes.why: **By + mốc quá khứ** cần quá khứ hoàn thành **had already built**, không phải hiện tại hoàn thành.

ieltsTips: Dùng **still** để mô tả vấn đề chưa được giải quyết, rất hợp với problem–solution: *Rural clinics **still** lack basic equipment despite a decade of investment.* Từ này ngầm khẳng định chính sách đã có nhưng chưa hiệu quả.

Dùng **have yet to + verb** để nói ai đó chưa làm gì, giọng trang trọng và có hàm ý phê bình: *The ministry **has yet to** publish the inspection report.* Hay hơn *has not published* trong ngữ cảnh học thuật.
Dùng **no longer** thay cho *not … any more* trong Writing để câu gọn và trang trọng: *Coal is **no longer** the cheapest option.* Ở vị trí giữa câu, nó cũng tránh được việc phải thêm trợ động từ.

Dùng **already** để nhấn mạnh tốc độ của một xu hướng: *By 2020, remote work had **already** become normal in the tech sector.* Cấu trúc *had already + V3* cho thấy bạn kiểm soát được thì quá khứ hoàn thành.

exercises.question: The waiting list ___ growing, despite extra funding.
The council has not published the figures ___.
Coal is ___ the cheapest source of electricity.
exercises.explanation: **no longer** in mid position = it has stopped being the cheapest.

exercises.question: By 2010, the city ___ its emissions target.
exercises.explanation: **By 2010** is a past deadline → past perfect **had already met**.

exercises.question: The shop doesn't open on Sundays ___ more.
exercises.explanation: **not … any more** — two words, end position.

exercises.question: The government has ___ to explain the delay.
exercises.explanation: **have yet to + verb** = have not yet done.

exercises.question: She has ___ left — you just missed her.
exercises.explanation: **already** in mid position after the auxiliary.

exercises.question: The factory is ___ operating; it closed last month.
___ yet, no study has tested the claim.
exercises.explanation: **As yet** = so far, formal academic phrase.
